notes: Baseline: the dataset's own system prompt, one call, no extra instructions.

Cheap prompt fix on the single-call baseline. Failures show 72/108 are overlaps (no end-time arithmetic), 'before X' misread as start<X (oodA-2878, oodA-2423 end past the deadline), and 9 no_json replies to chit-chat turns; the prompt now spells out constraint semantics, a place-then-verify method, a mandatory JSON-only reply, and a general soft-preference rule.

Structural change: plan-then-format. The parent's overlaps (72/108 failures) and wrong 'before X' handling come from answering JSON directly without arithmetic, and 9 failures were no-JSON replies to chit-chat; a planner now writes an explicit constraint table and HH:MM-HH:MM timeline with pairwise checks, and a formatter re-checks and emits JSON only.

Structural change: draft-then-verify. Evidence shows the parent's drafts are usually close (right events, mostly right constraints) but fail on overlaps (72/108) and end-time deadlines ('before X'); a verifier recomputes end times of the draft, flags violations and repairs with minimal moves, also catching no-JSON chit-chat replies. Risk: the final text contains reasoning before the JSON list, relying on the grader extracting the last list.

Structural: replace draft+verifier with extract-then-schedule. The parent's verifier re-reads the full conversation, re-derives constraints and then gets lost patching a bad draft until truncation (53 no_json failures); here an extractor (/no_think, no scheduling) produces a compact constraint+preference table and a scheduler that never sees the long conversation runs an earliest-deadline-first procedure, cutting tokens (~7.4k/sample, -0.15 fitness) and reasoning length. Preferences are normalised into windows/rules by the extractor so unseen preference types still flow through.

Prompt fix of the verifier. 31/37 dev_in and 22/30 ood_dev failures are no_json_list: the verifier rambles ('Wait - is there a gap we missed?'), debates infeasibility and hits max_tokens before ANSWER. The new verifier uses a compact per-event table (earliest start / latest end / preference window), a deterministic earliest-deadline-first rebuild instead of ad-hoc patching, an explicit 'a valid schedule always exists' cue, brevity instructions, and max_tokens raised 2500->4000.

Structural: add a cheap finalizer that never sees the conversation (only the blackboard) and must emit a bare JSON list. Evidence: 53 of 67 failures across splits are no_json_list because the verifier is truncated mid-reasoning; the finalizer salvages those by taking the ANSWER when present or else the draft plus the auditor's partial repairs. The verifier also gets the compact EDF-rebuild prompt (max_tokens 3000).

Merge draft+verifier into one native solver. The parent spends ~7.4k tokens/sample on two calls that each read the conversation, and the verifier mostly fails by getting truncated while patching a careless draft (53 no_json, 15 overlap/at fails). One role with a compact window table, an incremental cue (keep the previous reply's calendar and only move what the new request forces), deadline-first placement and a single timeline check costs about half the tokens and leaves no bad draft to anchor on. Unlike gen02_a1_child_3, no lossy extractor handoff.

Moves the reasoning into the draft. In the failure dump, 10/12 parseable dev_in drafts violated a rule (mostly one overlap): the one-shot JSON draft is careless, so the verifier spent its whole 2500-token budget re-deriving constraints and repairing, and got truncated (53 no_json). Now the draft writes a short window table, places events tightest-deadline-first and checks its timeline before the JSON. The verifier only checks one line per event, with a fast path that copies the calendar if every line is OK (max_tokens 3000).

Single-variable fix on the verifier budget plus brevity. 31/37 dev_in and 22/30 ood_dev failures are no_json_list: the failure dumps show the verifier cut off at 2500 tokens mid-audit (re-checking lines, 'wait...'), and the drafts it was fixing nearly always had one overlap. max_tokens 2500->4500 and one-line-per-event audits with no re-checking. The parent's minimal-move repair is kept (gen02_a1_child_1's EDF rebuild caused 24 conflicts).

Prompt fix of the verifier. Failure dumps show the verifier writing long prose constraint derivations ('start + duration <= 11:45 -> start <= 10:45 ...'), re-sorting the timeline twice, and even turning fuzzy preferences into hard rules ('afternoon' -> 'after 2 pm'); it then truncates (53/67 fails are no_json). Now a fixed one-line rule/check format with soft wishes kept out of hard ranges, a copy-through fast path when all lines are OK, and a gap-list repair; max_tokens 2500->3000 (not 4500, which a2_c1 showed only converts truncations into conflicts).

Structural: split the parent's verifier into a terse checker (max 1200, no fixing) and a repairer that only moves events the checker marked BAD into listed free gaps. The parent's single verifier spends its whole 2500-token budget re-deriving constraints in prose and is truncated before ANSWER (53/67 fails); separating the jobs gives each role a small, finishable task and the repairer has a fast copy path when VALID. The checker also keeps fuzzy wishes out of hard ranges (dumps show 'afternoon' turned into 'after 2 pm').

Structural: keep the parent's draft+verifier unchanged (it scores 0.63 when it finishes) and add a finalizer that sees the conversation plus both outputs. 53/67 parent failures are no_json because the verifier is truncated mid-audit; its partial audit (constraint list, marked overlaps) is still useful, so the finalizer continues from it with a short sorted-timeline check and always emits JSON. Unlike gen02_a1_child_2 the finalizer sees the conversation and the verifier keeps the parent's minimal-move repair (EDF rebuild caused conflicts).

Fire/merge: one native solver replaces draft+verifier. The parent spent ~7.4k-8.9k tokens/sample (about -0.16 fitness), and its verifier ran out of tokens on 53/67 failures without writing JSON; the draft step added little because its overlapping drafts were rebuilt anyway. A single bounded worksheet (windows table + greedy deadline-ordered placement) followed by JSON should roughly halve the tokens and remove the truncation failures.

Topology change: extract-then-schedule replaces draft-then-verify. Parent failures were the verifier mixing constraint parsing with open-ended search until it ran out of tokens (53/67 no_json_list). Here an extractor only builds a compact windows/preferences table, and the scheduler sees only that small table (not the full conversation), so it runs a bounded greedy earliest-deadline placement on cheap input; preferences stay generic as preferred windows/orderings.

Prompt fix of the verifier. 53 of 67 parent failures were no_json_list, all caused by the verifier rambling ('Wait... but...') until it hit max_tokens 2500 before writing ANSWER, even when the draft was already valid. The new verifier uses a bounded line-per-event format, a pass-through shortcut for valid drafts, a deterministic greedy rebuild (fixed events first, then earliest deadline), and a slightly larger token cap; preferences are handled generically as preferred windows.

Minimal fix of the parent. 53 of its 67 failures were no_json_list: the verifier was cut off at max_tokens 2500 while looping over repair ideas ('Wait... but...'), even though when it finished its answers were mostly correct. This child keeps both prompts unchanged except a raised verifier cap (4500) and one anti-looping rule that falls back to a deterministic latest-end-first rebuild after two failed repairs; earlier children that rewrote the whole verifier format lost accuracy, so the format is preserved.

Split the parent's verifier into auditor + repairer. Parent failures were 53/67 no_json_list: one verifier did constraint parsing, overlap search and repair in a single 2500-token budget and got truncated mid-search. Now a bounded auditor writes one line per event (window, optional preferred window, problem), and a repairer with its own budget either passes a valid draft through or repairs from the compact rule table, keeping OK events fixed; soft wishes are mapped generically to preferred windows.

Structural rescue role. 53 of 67 parent failures were no_json_list because the verifier was truncated before writing ANSWER, although its partial audit often already contained the fixes. A cheap finalizer now reads the draft plus the (possibly truncated) audit, copies the verifier answer when present, and otherwise completes the repair and emits JSON, so no sample ends without a calendar. Verifier prompt is untouched (cap 3000).

Cheap structural cut: fire the draft role and replace the verifier's open-ended audit-and-repair (which looped until truncation in 33/150 samples and averaged 8-10k tokens) with one native solver that follows a fixed window table + earliest-deadline-first placement with at most one restart. Drafts were overlap-ridden in nearly every failure, so they bought little; soft preferences are handled generally by turning any wish into a narrower window.

Split the work instead of audit-and-repair: an extractor turns the conversation into a compact constraint table, and a scheduler that never sees the conversation runs earliest-deadline-first on the table. Evidence: the parent verifier mixed re-reading the chat, checking a usually overlapping draft, and trial-and-error repairs, so it got truncated (33 no_json) and made arithmetic slips (e.g. a 30-min event written as 12:30-12:45). A short, focused context should keep both steps compact and cut tokens.

Minimal prompt fix of the parent. In the failures the verifier still looped over patch ideas until the 4500 cap (33 no_json) and slipped on durations; now any detected problem goes straight to the deterministic latest-end-first rebuild (one pass, one line per placement) instead of patching, with a worked arithmetic example. The cap is lowered to 3500 to cut tokens, since a non-looping rebuild fits easily.

Structural change: replace draft+free-form verifier with extract-then-schedule. The parent's no_json failures (33/50) come from the verifier mixing constraint parsing, auditing and repair in one long reply and running out of budget; here a short extractor emits a fixed constraint table (incl. a general pref field for unseen wish types) and the scheduler runs one greedy latest-end-first pass while tracking free gaps, which also targets the overlap/violates_at errors from mental arithmetic.

Cheap prompt fix. 33/50 failures are no_json: the verifier wrote long prose (event names, per-event 'soft preference' musings for events with none, re-checks) and hit the 3500 cap mid-rebuild. The audit is now a fixed terse per-event line format with a word budget, prefs only when stated, a 'move only the BAD event into a free gap' repair before the full rebuild (most failures are one newly added event overlapping), and an explicit >16:00 end example for the out_of_window misses.

Rescue topology. 33/50 parent failures are no_json because the verifier is truncated mid-rebuild, often with correct placement lines already written. A cheap finalizer always emits JSON: it copies the verifier's ANSWER when present, otherwise salvages the verifier's placement lines or the draft and patches the overlap. The verifier cap is cut to 2500 and its prose trimmed (prefs only when stated) to pay for the extra role.

Shift work upstream. The parent's draft emits bare JSON with no reasoning, so the verifier rebuilds often and the long rebuilds are what truncate (no_json) or misplace (overlap, violates_at). Here the draft writes a compact window table (hard windows from explicit times only, wishes as optional 'prefer' ranges) and does the latest-end-first placement itself, so the verifier usually only has to check a near-correct calendar against a table it can reuse, which should shorten its output.

Prompt fix of the verifier. Most remaining no_json failures (e.g. oodA-2423/2928/1871/112/2647) are the verifier looping 'but...' because it turned soft wishes (lunchtime, afternoon, end of day) or invented phrases into hard constraints, making the schedule look infeasible; now hard constraints come only from explicit times, the rebuild ignores wishes, and wishes are applied in a single free-gap pass afterwards. Also adds explicit end-by-16:00 checks (train-3019, oodA-717 placed events ending 16:15/16:30).

Budget hypothesis. Earlier children that cut the verifier's reasoning (terse audit, 2500 cap) lost far more on overlaps than they saved on no_json, so the reasoning is useful; the 33 no_json failures are mostly truncation at 3500 tokens mid-rebuild. This child keeps the parent prompt and raises the cap to 5000, adds a fast path (no problem -> answer immediately), and adds an escape rule (an 'impossible' schedule means a preference is blocking -> drop preferences), aimed at the 'but...' loops in oodA-2928/112/2647.

Merge/fire: tokens cost ~0.17 fitness (7.5k-9.6k per sample), largely the second call re-reading the whole conversation plus the draft. The draft adds little: in most failures the draft already overlapped and the verifier had to rebuild anyway. This child keeps one native-input planner that starts from its own previous turns, with the same table/check/rebuild procedure (prefs kept soft, swap repair, no 'impossible' loops) as the verifier fix, to test whether one call holds accuracy at roughly half the tokens.

Structural split: extract-then-solve. Failures mix constraint misreading (prefs promoted to hard in oodA-2423/717, wrong rule in train-3019/1305) with solver loops that truncate (7 no_json per split). An extractor turns the conversation into a numeric earliest/latest-end table with prefs separate and the previous start times; the scheduler sees only that table (not the conversation), cutting input tokens and keeping its reasoning purely arithmetic, with swap/gap-fill repair and a 'solution always exists' rule.

Prompt fix on the verifier. Failures show (a) fuzzy prefs promoted to hard rules (oodA-2423 'early in the day' -> impossible loop, oodA-717 vague 'after our sync' -> event placed at 16:00), (b) greedy deadline placement dead-ending on tight puzzles where an unconstrained event must fill an early gap (2423, train-207/1438), then 'but...' loops truncating to no_json. This child forces a numeric earliest/latest table with prefs in a separate column, adds a swap/gap-filling repair step and a 'a solution always exists' rule, bans reconsidering, and trims the cap to 4500 to cut tokens.

Cheap draft-prompt fix; verifier unchanged. Many failures start from a bad draft that the verifier must rebuild (and then loops/truncates): drafts drop earlier 'at' constraints (oodA-2981 lost 'at 2:30pm', train-1305 'at 12:30'), place events past 16:00 (oodA-717) or overlap. The draft now spells out the constraint rules, persistence across turns, the 16:00 end bound, and keeping prior times, so more samples take the verifier's no-problem fast path.

Verifier step-1 fix only, rest of parent verbatim (earlier children that rewrote the whole verifier collapsed). Evidence: the verifier lists 'no constraint (but was set to 12:30)' in train-1305 and misses 'at 2:30pm' in oodA-2981 (violates_at x6), and accepts 16:00-16:30 in oodA-717 after treating vague 'after our sync' as hard. Step 1 now scans every turn, maps set/lock/move/slot-to-X to 'at', says constraints persist, flags end>16:00, and says fuzzy wishes never justify leaving the day.

Structural: parent unchanged plus a second audit pass (same proven verifier procedure, 4000 cap) that reads the verifier's ANSWER and the conversation. 14 no_json failures are verifier truncations and 17 are overlaps it let through; a fresh auditor can rebuild from the conversation when the ANSWER is missing and take the fast path when it is already fine. Tests whether ~2-3k extra tokens buy more than the 0.05 token penalty.

Token cut on the draft plus the arithmetic check. Tokens cost ~0.17 fitness and the verifier rebuilds most bad drafts anyway (a2_c1 showed draft quality barely matters), so the draft gets /no_think, a 1200 cap, and is told to keep previous times and list events by start so the verifier's sorted audit is trivial. The verifier keeps the parent prompt except step 2's explicit hour+minute end arithmetic and neighbour-pair overlap check (train-94/2432 passed miscomputed overlaps).

Soft-preference mechanism fix. ood_dev has 5 soft_miss failures (oodA-1903/2928/3781/1177/2217) plus overlaps where prefs were half-applied: the parent's fast path only 'moves one event if obviously safe', so most unmet prefs are ignored, and prefs phrased indirectly ('my mornings are for deep work', 'toward the end of my day') or about earlier-turn events are missed. Step 1 now gives a general recipe to convert any fuzzy wish into a window (never hard), and step 3's no-problem path tries each unmet pref by moving that one event into a free gap with a neighbour check.

Cheap verifier arithmetic fix, rest of parent verbatim. Failures show the verifier's step-2 audit passing overlaps because it miscomputes ends (train-94 wrote 13:45-14:00 for a 75-min event; train-2432 accepted 13:15-14:15 next to 13:45; train-1005 listed out of order) and declaring the fast path. Step 2 now spells out hour+minute end arithmetic with worked examples and an explicit neighbour-pair 'end <= next start?' check, and the rebuild lines reuse it.

Verifier gets /no_think and a 3500 cap. 20/150 parent failures are no_json_list: the verifier rambles ('but wait', 'reconsider') until the 5000-token cap and never reaches ANSWER (train-1005, train-438, oodA-717). The numbered audit/rebuild steps already give visible step-by-step reasoning, so hidden thinking is redundant; this should cut tokens sharply and force terse single-pass rebuilds.

Structural change: replace the draft calendar with a /no_think constraint-sheet extractor, and have a thinking scheduler place events from scratch in integer minutes-from-10:00. Evidence: the verifier rebuilt most drafts anyway, and most hard failures are arithmetic/overlap slips in HH:MM (train-207, train-1438, oodA-876 miscomputed ends) or mis-read constraints (train-2329 invented 'before 11am'). Soft wishes are mapped to a generic preferred window/relation so unseen preference types are still handled.

Adds a cheap /no_think finalizer after the verifier and trims the verifier cap to 4000. no_json_list is the single largest failure (20/150): the verifier gets truncated mid-rebuild (train-1005, train-3019, oodA-717, oodA-1871) and emits nothing. The finalizer copies the ANSWER when present and otherwise salvages the partial placements plus draft into valid JSON.

Cheap prompt fix on the verifier for the dominant failure: 20/150 no_json_list where the verifier decides the problem is impossible and loops until the cap (train-1005, train-3507, oodA-1871, oodA-2217 'impossible to schedule'), often because of a misread constraint (train-2329 invented 'before 11am', oodA-2559 read 'at 2pm' as 'after 2pm'). Step 1 now must quote the user's exact words per event, the prompt states every instance is solvable, and step 3 gets a single bounded fallback that always ends in an ANSWER. Draft and topology unchanged.

Structural change to the repair algorithm: replace 'rebuild everything' with gap-based minimal repair (keep valid events, list free gaps, slot only the bad events into gaps), falling back to a single full rebuild. Evidence: the draft keeps prior-turn events valid, so most failures involve just 1-2 conflicting events, yet full rebuilds spiral into long 'impossible' loops (train-1005, train-1361, oodA-1871 no_json) or introduce new overlaps (train-1305, train-207). Constraints are normalised to explicit [earliest start, latest end] windows with quoted user words to stop misreads like oodA-2559 'at 2pm'->after.

Targets ood_dev, where 7 of the 24 failures are soft_miss (score 0.5-0.75: oodA-2928, oodA-942, oodA-3511 left preferred events outside 'early'/'midday'/'end of day' windows) because the verifier only moves events for preferences when 'obviously safe' and drops them in rebuilds. The draft now honours wishes, and the verifier turns every wish into a generic checkable target (window OR relation, so unseen preference types still map) that it actively repairs and places before unconstrained events in rebuilds. It also quotes the user's exact words and has a bounded fallback that always reaches ANSWER, addressing the no_json loops.

Shifts effort to the draft. 11 of 12 dev_in failure drafts I checked were broken (mostly a single overlap from the new event: train-1005, train-438, train-207), and those broken drafts send the verifier into long rebuilds that loop to the cap. The draft now thinks briefly with a per-event rule ledger and wish windows so the verifier usually takes the cheap 'no problem' path; the verifier cap drops to 4500 and the 'drop preferences when impossible' clause is removed.

Structural change to how the verifier represents time: a 24-slot quarter-hour grid instead of HH:MM end arithmetic. Overlaps and wrong ends still slip through (train-207, train-1305, train-739 overlaps passed as OK; train-438/oodA-1871 miscomputed free gaps while rebuilding then looped to the cap). With a grid, overlaps are two ids in one slot and free gaps are runs of '-', so both audit and rebuild become lookups rather than arithmetic; the 'drop preferences when impossible' clause is replaced by a bounded move-one-event retry.

Verifier-only prompt fix for the rebuild algorithm. 13/24 parent failures are no_json loops where the deadline-ordered greedy rebuild got stuck (train-1005, train-1361, oodA-1871) and the model spiralled into 'impossible'; oodA-1871 also skipped event 0's 'at 3:30pm'. Step 1 now walks turns in order and normalises each event into an [E, L] window, step 3 orders by slack (most constrained first), lists free gaps after each placement, and has a concrete bounded bump rule instead of 'drop preferences'.

Structural change: replace the full-JSON draft with a /no_think constraint extractor that writes a compact id|name|duration|window|pref table, and have the final role always schedule from scratch with EDF. Evidence: most no_json loops (train-1361, 1438, 2733, 183, oodA-2217) come from the verifier anchoring on the draft's (often overlapping) times and treating them as fixed; with no draft there is nothing to anchor on, and the table also makes general preference types explicit for the scheduler. Lower scheduler cap (4000) plus a cheaper first role should cut tokens.

Token + preference play. The verifier gets /no_think, a terse format and a 4000 cap (tokens cost ~0.17 fitness), plus the anti-anchoring rule (only 'at' immovable, soft never infeasible) that the no_json loops (train-1438, 2733, oodA-717) lacked. Preferences are generalized (order, gaps, grouping, avoidance) and pushed into both roles: the draft now places events to satisfy soft wishes, and the verifier rebuilds when a wish is unmet using hard∩soft windows, targeting the 0.72 soft_mean (oodA-3781, 876, 942 placed by earliest-fit ignoring prefs).

Prompt-only fix of the verifier. 20/150 failures were no_json: the verifier looped until the 5000-token cap because it treated the draft's times (train-1361, 1438, 2733, oodA-2217) or soft wishes (oodA-717 'after our sync') as fixed and concluded 'impossible'. The new prompt states draft times are guesses, only 'at' is fixed, prefs never cause infeasibility, lists explicit windows, and gives a bounded fallback ladder (prefs -> hard only -> any gap). Rebuild also uses pref∩hard windows, since soft misses (oodA-3781, 876, 195) came from earliest-fit packing ignoring prefs.

Prompt-only verifier fix. 20/150 failures are no_json: the verifier misses constraints set in earlier turns (oodA-1871 lost 'at 3:30pm' for event 0 and 'after 1:45pm' for event 3), concludes the day is infeasible and loops to the cap (train-1005, 2733, 3507, oodA-2217). Step 1 now walks every user message, and step 3 states a valid calendar always exists, so impossibility means a blocking preference or a misread rule, with a hard stop after one retry. Everything else is unchanged.

Structural: the cheap /no_think draft now writes an explicit per-event RULES ledger (walking every user message) before its JSON, and the verifier audits that ledger instead of re-extracting from scratch. Evidence: no_json loops start from constraints missed in earlier turns (oodA-1871 dropped event 0 'at 3:30pm' and event 3 'after 1:45pm'; train-2329, 3507 debated whether rules were soft), after which the verifier believes the day is infeasible and burns its 5000-token cap. The ledger is also how new preference types get stated in general form.

Shift reasoning to the draft. The verifier only fails badly when it has to rebuild (all 20 no_json cases had a bad /no_think draft it then could not repair, e.g. oodA-1871 with three events at 15:30), so the draft now thinks (cap 3000) and should usually pass step 2 unchanged, making the verifier short. The verifier gets one extra line: a valid calendar always exists and an answer is mandatory.
